previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: An elderly female with a history of GERD, chronic diastolic heart failure (EF 55–60%), chronic microcytic anemia, and chronic pulmonary embolism on warfarin presented with odynophagia described as burning from the mouth to the esophagus, triggered by eating beans and associated with heartburn. She had no nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain. In the ED, her symptoms improved with IV pantoprazole and a GI cocktail. A transient drop in oxygen saturation to 91% on room air prompted a chest X-ray, which showed mild-to-moderate pulmonary edema and cardiomegaly, leading to a diagnosis of acute on chronic diastolic heart failure. She received one dose of IV furosemide and was admitted for observation. Her symptoms resolved, oxygen stabilized at 94% on room air, and she tolerated oral intake. Chronic microcytic anemia was stable with no signs of active bleeding. Warfarin was held briefly due to supratherapeutic INR and resumed at 2 mg daily. Asymptomatic bacteriuria was noted with urine culture pending. She was discharged home the following day with instructions to continue her baseline medications, use over-the-counter Tums for heartburn as needed, monitor daily weight, and follow up with her PCP and gastroenterologist.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Other nonspecific findings on examination of urine

INDICATION:  Chest pain, assess for pneumonia.

TECHNIQUE:  Portable AP upright radiograph of the chest.

COMPARISONS:  Chest radiograph ___.

FINDINGS:  Pulmonary vascular indistinctness and septal lines suggest
mild-to-moderate pulmonary edema with stable cardiomegaly.  Retrocardiac
opacification could reflect atelectasis and effusion.  Small right effusion
may also be present.
